report:
## Research Findings: Abaloparatide and Vertebral Fracture Reduction

The claim is well-supported by high-quality evidence.

**Pivotal trial evidence:** The ACTIVE trial (Abaloparatide Comparator Trial In Vertebral Endpoints), a randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator (teriparatide)-controlled Phase 3 study in ambulatory postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, found that 18 months of daily subcutaneous abaloparatide (80 mcg) significantly reduced new morphometric vertebral fractures by 86% compared with placebo (p<0.001), with an absolute risk reduction of 3.6%. Nonvertebral fractures were also reduced by roughly 43% (JAMA, 2016: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640).

**Confirmation and extension:** Subgroup analyses stratified by FRAX fracture probability confirmed the benefit persisted across baseline risk categories, with significant reductions in vertebral, nonvertebral, and major osteoporotic fractures versus placebo, and even versus teriparatide for some endpoints (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6373333/). The follow-up ACTIVExtend study, in which women transitioned to alendronate after abaloparatide or placebo, showed continued low vertebral fracture rates in the abaloparatide-to-alendronate group versus placebo-to-alendronate, with a 71% relative risk reduction sustained over extended follow-up (PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31674644/).

**Independent synthesis:** A network meta-analysis pooling ACTIVE and other osteoporosis trials concluded that abaloparatide reduces vertebral, nonvertebral, and wrist fracture risk versus placebo and compares favorably with other approved therapies (Osteoporosis International: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00198-019-04947-2).

**Regulatory status:** Based on this evidence, the FDA approved abaloparatide (Tymlos) specifically for postmenopausal women at high fracture risk (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208743lbl.pdf).

**Conclusion:** The evidence—from a well-designed RCT, subgroup analyses, extension studies, and independent meta-analysis—robustly supports that abaloparatide reduces vertebral fracture risk in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis. The claim is true.
